symptom: every unit write, and every statement of a run that holds its writes, parsed the whole document four times to give it its storage form: Writer.normalizeForStorage was 1.4 s of 8.2 s sampled when seeding 300 entities and 299 associations (ako/mxcli#2160)
cause: the storage form is four passes - StripUndeclaredProperties, CompletePropertySets, FillMissingUserRoleGUIDs, NormalizeListMarkers - each a function from bytes to bytes that unmarshals the document and, when it changes something, marshals it again. Each was added for its own defect and is correct alone; called in a row they pay for the document once each
insight: Sharing one parse is not obviously the same thing: a later pass then walks values the earlier one appended in memory, which have not been through an encode and a decode, and the walkers switch on decoded types (bson.A, int32). So the old sequence is kept as the definition (completeForStorageInPasses, also the fallback for a document that does not parse) and the new function is compared with it byte for byte on every PedApp unit, as stored and with properties left out, at four versions: 7,380 comparisons, identical. The first version of that test was green with two of the four passes removed from the new function: PedApp has no user role without a GUID, and this package's tests register no list markers, so both passes were inert on both sides. Removing each pass in turn is what showed it; the test now builds a variant per pass and asserts each pass had something to do. A differential test proves equality only over the inputs that make the two sides do something. Version lowering stays a separate call: it returns without parsing on a version that has every shape, and a test stubs it. Measured: 4 parses -> 1 per unit; the entity seed 7.2 s -> 6.3 s first run and about 9 s -> 7.6 s settled re-run; the 600-page seed 36.6 s -> 33.1 s; output identical to the previous binary on all five runs.
